claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind (per kind_sorter.go); chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's install order is a hardcoded list of Kubernetes kinds in the Helm source, beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-ordered list in reverse.
Helm sends the sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies don't change ordering: a subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so a chart can't express installing one subchart before another.
Resources created by Helm chart hooks are not managed by Helm as part of the release; hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
Passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in Pulumi's dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating resources that depend on it, and deploys independent resources in parallel.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.
helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of using Pulumi and Helm together.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program with helm.v4.Chart or helm.v3.Release is the most common adoption pattern.
helm.v4.Chart renders chart templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object as an individual Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release in the cluster, preserving chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by Kubernetes kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Pulumi installs a chart after the resources it depends on, resolving values at deploy time.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order with each resource ready before dependents, unlike Helm's fixed order by kind.
